newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City calls smog alert, orders cars off roads.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City calls smog alert, orders cars off roads.

text.p: Nearly half the cars in Mexico City were ordered to keep off the roads on Wednesday and schools told to keep children inside amid soaring smog levels in one of the world's dirtiest cities, officials said on Tuesday.
The largest factories in this city of 18 million residents must also cut production by at least 40 percent after levels of ozone on Tuesday rose to more than twice the allowable international limits.

Mexico City's Environment Commission said it implemented the first phase of a pollution alert after ozone hit 256 points in the southwestern part of the city. The World Health Organisation says anything more than one hour of exposure per year to ozone above 100 points is dangerous to human health.

Ozone is a dangerous pollutant that results when car fumes mix with radiation from the sun. Exhaust from Mexico City's more than 3 million cars often gets trapped along with other noxious fumes in this bowl-shaped valley.
Mexico City residents cannot drive their cars one day a week under normal conditions. During pollution emergencies, residents cannot drive two of the five workdays.
